q: Does the compact 2e ansatz retain its expressiveness advantage when replaced by / compared against modern adaptive ansatze (ADAPT-VQE, iterative-QCC, qubit-ADAPT) on the same H2/STO-3G target, and — critically — on non-trivial two-electron systems like HeH+ or H2 in larger bases (6-31G, cc-pVDZ) where adaptive selection can grow the operator pool?
basis: Paper predates the adaptive-ansatz literature explosion (ADAPT-VQE, Grimsley et al. 2019; qubit-ADAPT, Tang et al. 2021). Our replication confirms C1 in the trivial STO-3G regime where any expressiveness-complete ansatz reaches FCI; the interesting comparison is in larger active spaces where adaptive methods dynamically grow parameter count. C6's 3x parameter reduction vs UCCSD may vanish or invert against ADAPT.
next_steps: Reuse existing PySCF + OpenFermion pipeline. Add openfermion.circuits.uccsd_singlet + a from-scratch ADAPT-VQE loop on H2 in {STO-3G, 6-31G, cc-pVDZ} and on HeH+/LiH (2e active space). Score (i) final energy vs FCI, (ii) parameter count at chemical-accuracy convergence, (iii) CNOT count under a common transpilation policy. Free endpoints only: local Qiskit statevector, no hardware. Deliverable: a 4-column expressiveness/economy table.

q: How does the compact ansatz's noise-free-perfect FCI-reachability degrade under a realistic device noise model (depolarising, amplitude-damping, and measurement error at NISQ-era rates), with and without symmetry verification / zero-noise extrapolation / readout mitigation — and does the 6-CNOT vs 8-CNOT vs 14-CNOT gap in circuit depth actually translate to the fidelity gap the paper implies?
basis: Paper's central practical value proposition is C4+C5: hardware runs on ibm-5/ibm-14 reach mhartree accuracy WITH error mitigation. Our replication cannot exercise this — both devices are retired. But the ansatz-vs-noise interaction is testable on Qiskit's noise-model simulator, which is a free endpoint. Without this, the CNOT-savings argument is unfalsified.
next_steps: Build a Qiskit Aer noise model calibrated to published ibm-5 / ibm-14 gate + readout error rates (retrievable from IBM Quantum device backend calibration snapshots archived on GitHub or the Qiskit Metadata Provider). Sweep depolarising rate p ∈ [1e-4, 1e-2] × (compact-6CNOT, compact-8CNOT, UCCSD-14CNOT) × {no-mitigation, ZNE, symmetry-verify}. Metric: |E_noisy - E_FCI| vs p. Free: Aer local. Deliverable: 3x3 heatmap of accuracy floor.

q: Does the compact ansatz's expressiveness transfer across bond-length regimes when the natural-orbital basis is fixed at one geometry (say R=0.735 A) vs re-optimised per geometry, and how does the transferability error compare with the transferability of the parameter θ itself?
basis: Ansatz relies on natural-orbital (Zumino) basis. Our replication silently re-solves NOs at every R via PySCF's per-geometry HF. In a realistic pipeline (e.g. reactive dynamics), you'd want to fix the basis once and vary θ, or use active-space embedding with a frozen NO basis. The paper does not report this decomposition; it is an open transferability question directly implied by the ansatz form.
next_steps: Modify vqe_h2_compact.py to accept a --nocap R0 flag: run RHF+NOs once at R0, then for each R build the Hamiltonian in that FROZEN NO basis and re-optimise only θ. Compare energy error vs FCI(re-optimised NOs at R) across R ∈ [0.5, 3.0]. Report the transferability window (how far can R drift from R0 before the frozen-basis compact ansatz misses chemical accuracy?). Free: local PySCF. Deliverable: transferability curve.

q: When the compact 2e ansatz is embedded into an active-space method (CASSCF / DMRG-based orbital selection / SHCI) for a larger molecule with a 2e active space carved out, does the sub-ppm accuracy of the ansatz on the active-space projected Hamiltonian survive, or does the orbital-selection error dominate the ansatz error?
basis: The compact 2e ansatz is only useful in production if it can be plugged into an embedding wrapper for molecules bigger than H2. The paper does not exercise this. Given our sub-picohartree ansatz error, the practical accuracy floor will be set entirely by CASSCF/DMRG orbital selection — this is a testable hypothesis.
next_steps: Use PySCF's CASSCF(2,2) on H2O (freeze 8 electrons, 2 active) and on LiH; compute (i) FCI-in-active-space reference, (ii) compact-VQE-in-active-space energy, (iii) full-molecule CCSD(T) reference. Decompose the error as [active-space projection] + [ansatz]. Free: PySCF local. Deliverable: error-decomposition table for 3-4 test molecules.

q: Can an ML classifier (or symbolic-regression / graph-neural-network) trained on {molecule, basis, geometry, target-accuracy} predict which of {compact-2e, UCCSD, k-UpCCGSD, ADAPT-VQE, hardware-efficient} is the best ansatz choice — and does the compact-2e ansatz occupy a distinct region of the feature space (2-electron, small basis, non-adaptive) that ML can cleanly identify?
basis: Given the proliferation of VQE ansatze (compact-2e, UCCSD, k-UpCCGSD, ADAPT-VQE, HEA, ...) each with its own sweet spot, ansatz selection is currently manual and heuristic. If the compact-2e ansatz has a well-defined applicability envelope (=exactly 2 electrons, small basis, near-equilibrium), that envelope should be ML-discoverable. This informs whether the paper's contribution is a niche tool or a general primitive.
next_steps: Build a small dataset of (molecule, basis, R, best-ansatz-by-accuracy-at-chemaccuracy-budget) tuples across {H2, HeH+, H3+, LiH, BeH2} × {STO-3G, 6-31G} × {ADAPT-VQE, compact-2e where applicable, UCCSD}. Train a small XGBoost / decision-tree classifier; report feature-importance. Free: sklearn local. Deliverable: decision-tree diagram identifying the compact-2e applicability envelope.
